doc.title: Buddy Collette interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

chapter: Studio work and Stars of Swing
title: Why the Stars of Swing was never recorded; Spaulding Givens's 'Laura'
summary: Record companies could not categorize the band; he describes the difficult interwoven 'Laura' arrangement.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: It’s a shame. The record people came in and heard it and they didn’t know what to call it.
They were afraid, they said what can we call it? They said well it sounds okay, but what is it? It was just good music. They didn’t want that.
Post-bop? I guess it was too early for post-bop, huh?

Yeah. But anyway it was a great band. I wish they had recorded it. But we did do an album, we did two sides I think, “Laura” is one, when “Laura” had come out, Spaulding did an arrangement of “Laura,” it was unbelievable, the arrangement, with the four horns. He had them, the way he wrote it, he’d be playing the melody and then another horn would just take it off and, the way it was interwoven between the different horns. And for a while we couldn’t play it. We could read it but it just wouldn’t work. Because he had this crazy idea that it would work if we just listened to each other and got used to it. And he was right. Because we had to keep trying to play it. And finally we’d say well now you’re playing too strong there, and then they’d have to listen and finally know that you had the next part that would take over the melody. And if one person didn’t do it right it wouldn’t work.
